title: Salary Packaging Health Industry: Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay Under the National Minimum Wage and Awards
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Compare the National Minimum Wage with award rates, casual loading, and super. Includes salary pack
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour, giving $52,254.80/year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, super, and any deductions. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05/hour (base $26.44 + 25%). When converting to annual pay, use the loaded rate in the formula. Note that super is paid on the loaded rate as well.

faqs.q: How does salary packaging work in the health industry?
faqs.a: Salary packaging health industry arrangements allow employees to sacrifice part of their pre-tax salary for benefits such as private health insurance, medical expenses, or car parking. This reduces your taxable income but does not affect the hourly-to-annual conversion itself. The annual figure calculated from your hourly rate is your gross salary before any packaging deductions. For specific limits and rules, consult the Australian Taxation Office or your employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly Rate and Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, converting it to an annual figure helps you compare jobs, budget, and plan tax. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the common benchmark), the calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This gives you the gross amount before tax, the Medicare levy, and superannuation. It assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If your hours differ, replace 38 with your actual weekly hours.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage (NMW) as the legal floor. From 1 July 2026, the NMW is **$26.44 per hour** for a permanent employee, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. For casual workers, a 25% loading applies, making the minimum **$33.05 per hour**.

However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. Award rates vary by classification, experience, and shift. For example, a health industry award might pay more than the NMW for a registered nurse or an administrative officer. The NMW is the absolute minimum; your actual rate may be higher. To check your award, visit the Fair Work Ombudsman website or use our [pay guides](/blog) for industry-specific information.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual, personal, or public holidays). When converting a casual rate to annual pay, use the loaded rate in the formula. For example, a casual on the NMW would calculate $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,310.80 per year.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). Your employer must pay this into your super fund; it is not deducted from your pay. So if your annual gross is $65,310.80, your employer contributes an additional $7,837.30 in super (12% of $65,310.80, assuming no cap applies).

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To estimate your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a 38‑hour week at $26.44/hour, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80. This can help you align with bills and rent cycles.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not yet confirmed). For a full‑time worker on the NMW ($52,254.80), the tax would be approximately $7,267 (based on the 2026–27 scale) plus Medicare of $1,045.10 (2% of $52,254.80), leaving about $43,942.70 after tax and Medicare. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more precise estimate.

### Salary Packaging in the Health Industry

If you work in the health sector, you may be eligible for **salary packaging health industry** arrangements. This allows you to sacrifice part of your pre‑tax salary for benefits such as private health insurance, medical expenses, or car parking. Salary packaging reduces your taxable income, which can lower your tax bill. However, it does not change the hourly‑to‑annual conversion itself—your gross annual figure remains the same before packaging. The packaged amount is deducted from your salary before tax, so your take‑home pay may be higher than a simple tax calculation suggests. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Comparing the NMW with Award Rates

The NMW is a safety net, but many awards set higher rates. For example, the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020 has minimum rates above the NMW for most classifications. If you are covered by an award, your hourly rate will be at least the award rate for your role. The NMW is not a job median; it is the legal minimum. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full‑time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 per year—well above the NMW. That figure is an average across all industries, not a median for a specific job. For your own role, check your award or enterprise agreement.

### Important Disclaimer

This conversion is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is not a determination of your pay or tax. For personalised advice, consult a tax professional.

### Quick Reference

- **National Minimum Wage (permanent):** $26.44/hour, $1,004.90/week, $52,254.80/year
- **National Minimum Wage (casual):** $33.05/hour, $1,255.90/week, $65,310.80/year
- **ABS Average Weekly Earnings (full‑time adult ordinary time):** $2,083.70/week (average, not median)
- **Super guarantee:** 12% on top, up to $270,830
- **Tax‑free threshold:** $18,200

Use our [reference tables](/data) for more conversions and our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for the latest rates. If you need to calculate your own pay, try [the timesheet](/) on our home page—just enter your base hourly rate and tick the casual loading box if applicable.
